page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.re6p-redis.2xlarge is an x86_64 instance configuration equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The processor architecture includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 instruction sets, including VNNI. The system provides 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage, operating purely via remote network-attached disks, and features a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps under the KVM hypervisor without hardware GPU acceleration.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the middle tier across compute and memory categories. The CPU achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,486.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 8,313.72, while single-core output is modest, recording 1,178.0 in Geekbench and 1,318.98 in stress-ng. Memory subsystems achieve 50.58 GB/sec uncached read throughput and 38.0 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth, which supports Redis caching throughput measured at 6.81 million SET operations per second and a PassMark database operations score of 2,849.77.

Because the server lacks onboard ephemeral NVMe drives, I/O-intensive workloads depend entirely on network storage, which must share the 2 Gbps network baseline. From a resource perspective, the configuration offers balanced memory density and dedicated CPU allocation without the overhead of unused accelerator hardware. This profile is engineered primarily for in-memory caching systems such as Redis, moderate transactional database instances, and general-purpose backend services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.re6p-redis.2xlarge is an x86_64 server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 35 MB of L3 cache, and 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The configuration includes no local storage or GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached block devices alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations place the instance within the mid-range tier, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,486.0, uncached memory read bandwidth of 50.58 GB/sec, and Redis throughput of 6.81 million SET operations per second. Lacking bundled NVMe disks, disk operations rely on external volumes constrained by baseline network limits. The instance is suitable for distributed in-memory caching, Redis deployments, mid-scale relational databases, and general application serving.
